questions.q: What is FA-10452's January depreciation charge as currently categorized (Office Equipment, 5-year life)?
questions.explain: $145,000.00 divided by 60 months (5 years) equals $2,416.67 per month.

questions.q: What would FA-10452's correct January depreciation be under Manufacturing Equipment's 10-year life?
questions.explain: $145,000.00 divided by 120 months (10 years) equals $1,208.33 per month.

questions.q: What is the exact dollar overstatement in January's depreciation expense caused by the miscategorization?
questions.explain: $2,416.67 minus $1,208.33 leaves a $1,208.34 overstatement for January.

questions.q: Why doesn't the depreciation program flag or fail on this calculation?
options: It does fail, and requires manual override
Oracle Fusion Assets does not calculate depreciation for new categories in their first month
The program only runs depreciation for assets over $500,000
The program calculates correctly against the category data it was given — it has no way to know the category itself was wrong
questions.explain: Straight-line depreciation is calculated correctly based on the asset's assigned category — the program has no way to detect that the category assignment itself is a business error.

questions.q: Why does this lesson emphasize that the error is 'recurring,' not one-time?
options: Because the same overstated amount posts every single month the asset remains miscategorized, compounding over time
Because it only affects the Canadian ledger
Because it reverses automatically after one period
Because it only occurs on leap years
questions.explain: Unlike a single wrong invoice, a depreciation miscategorization repeats every period until corrected, which is why catching it early matters.
